clue.text: Climber creating a system of tracks on small mountain

parts.note: a hill is a modest mountain
RY is the standard abbreviation for railway, a system of tracks

explanation.surface: Someone lays out a railway network on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the hill first. Sir Edmund Hillary, with Tenzing Norgay, made the first ascent of Everest in 1953.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Hillary was the famous New Zealand mountaineer who first summited Everest.

clue.text: Follow the example of one Christian, say, about it

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: about here means going around, so the mate's letters surround the next piece

parts.note: Fletcher Christian of the Bounty mutiny was a master's mate, so he exemplifies a ship's mate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A churchgoer urges copying the ways of a fellow believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' reads as a believer, but it is Fletcher Christian, the master's mate who led the mutiny on HMS Bounty; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone is to model your conduct on theirs, the same as following their example.

clue.text: Composer's piece of subtle harmony

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musical work by some composer is praised for its delicate harmonies.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Composer's' links definition and wordplay: the composer's (name is a) piece of the phrase. Franz Lehár wrote the operetta The Merry Widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was the Hungarian composer of operettas such as The Merry Widow.

clue.text: About to punish, in a way, monarch who makes improvements?

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
fining is one way to punish someone
R stands for rex or regina, a monarch

explanation.surface: A king who punishes his subjects with fines is wryly called a reformer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the loose definition: a refiner purifies metal or sugar, so in a sense improves it.
explanation.definitionFit: A refiner is someone who purifies or polishes things, a person who makes improvements.

clue.text: Pound and a shilling I laid out to see early movie great

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
taken as written

indicators.note: laid out means spent, and also set out in a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spends a pound and a shilling on a ticket to watch a silent-film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid out' looks like money spent, but it rearranges L, A, SHILLING and I. A shilling is an old British coin worth one twentieth of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Lillian Gish was a leading actress of the silent era, starring in films such as Intolerance.

clue.text: Ruler in Asian country heading changes out East

definitions.text: Ruler in Asian country heading changes out East

indicators.note: in puts the ruler inside the name of the country

parts.note: India is a country in South Asia
R is a common abbreviation for a ruler, rex or regina

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the word heading are reshuffled
out says one letter is put out of the reshuffle, leaving it behind

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A leader takes power in an Asian nation and sweeps away the old guard in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into INDIA; then HEADING, with E sent 'out', is rearranged ('changes') into the surname. The whole clue also describes her: a ruler in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Indira Gandhi was Prime Minister of India, a ruler of that Asian country.

clue.text: Experiences awful situation that's potentially explosive

parts.note: to live something is to experience it, as in living through a war
hell is any dreadful situation

explanation.surface: Someone goes through a terrible ordeal on the verge of blowing up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a person about to explode with anger; the answer is unexploded ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: A live shell is ammunition still armed and capable of detonating.

clue.text: Over small area, abolishes certain plants

indicators.note: over says the abolishing word is placed over, covering, the next piece

parts.note: to annul something is to cancel or abolish it
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A council scraps a small patch of planting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' puts ANNULS round A, the abbreviation for area.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuals are plants that complete their life cycle within a single year.

clue.text: For example, 5 10, 12 22, 13 and 18; or 6 24 and 15 — and 1 29, maybe

definitions.text: For example, 5 10, 12 22, 13 and 18; or 6 24 and 15 — and 1 29, maybe

parts.words: For example, 5 10, 12 22, 13 and 18; or 6 24 and 15 — and 1 29, maybe
parts.note: the film stars headlined pictures, the stateswomen headed governments, and the last named, a would-be president, might yet lead

explanation.surface: A list of famous women grouped by what they shared.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works in two senses: star actresses (Gish, Bacall, Day, West) and women who led nations (Gandhi, Meir); 'maybe' covers Hillary Clinton, then a presidential hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both principal actresses in films and, read literally, women who lead countries.

clue.text: See 5
There's no time for this in the Olympics, for example

definitions.text: There's no time for this in the Olympics, for example

parts.words: There's no time for this in the Olympics, for example
parts.note: the surface suggests a busy schedule, but means a contest such as the javelin or long jump, judged by distance or height rather than by a clock

explanation.surface: An Olympic event so crowded that there is no slot for it in the timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Throws and jumps are measured, not timed, unlike track races.
explanation.definitionFit: Field events like shot put and high jump are scored by measurement rather than stopwatch.

clue.text: Rewrite a banal clue by learner about queen or film star

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters plus the learner go around the queen
rewrite says the words of the dull clue are recast in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the learner driver's plate abbreviation
R stands for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A novice is told to redo a dull crossword clue about royalty or celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rewrite' rearranges A BANAL CLUE into LAUENBACAL; add L; 'about' places that round R. Lauren Bacall starred in To Have and Have Not.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauren Bacall was a Hollywood actress, famous opposite Humphrey Bogart.

clue.text: Run into party with one's date, an actress

parts.note: a do is a party or social gathering
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
one's is read as one is, IS
a day is a date on the calendar

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into a party with their date, a starlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', giving IS. Doris Day starred in Calamity Jane and Pillow Talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Day was an American actress and singer of 1950s and 60s film musicals and comedies.

clue.text: Making poor start — finally good fish caught

indicators.note: caught says the fish is held inside the word for start

parts.note: to begin is to start
the gar is a long-snouted fish

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of good

explanation.surface: A fisherman starts badly, landing his catch only at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making poor' is the definition, not a description of the start; 'caught' signals the fish held inside, and 'finally' takes the last letter of 'good'.
explanation.definitionFit: To beggar someone is to reduce them to poverty, so beggaring is impoverishing.

clue.text: Leave a milder recollection of so-called Iron Lady

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: recollection is read as re-collection, gathering the letters together again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gentler memory of a formidable woman politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollection' is read as re-collection, rearranging A MILDER into LDAMEIR. 'Iron Lady' suggests Thatcher, but Golda Meir earned the nickname first.
explanation.definitionFit: Golda Meir, Israel's Prime Minister, was described as the Iron Lady of Israeli politics.

clue.text: Animal first across threshold of ark

indicators.note: across says the word for first stretches over and around the next letter

parts.note: best means first, top of the class

indicators.note: the threshold is the entrance, so the opening letter of ark

explanation.surface: The first creature to step aboard Noah's ark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' looks like an order of boarding but means BEST; 'threshold of ark' is A.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is any animal, especially a large four-footed one.

clue.text: Fish was far from fresh!

definitions.meaning: gave off a stink, as stale food does

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the fish was off.
explanation.definitionFit: Smelt names a small fish and is also the British past tense of smell, meaning stank.

clue.text: She was prominent at the front as a wartime life-saver

definitions.text: She was prominent at the front
definitions.meaning: a Hollywood star famous for her ample bust, so prominent at the front
RAF airmen named their inflatable life jackets after that buxom actress

explanation.surface: A woman stood out on the front line as a heroine who saved lives in the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the front' suggests a battle front, but it is her figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Mae West was a curvaceous screen star, and the Second World War inflatable life vest carried her name.

clue.text: Organising big, nothing small?

indicators.note: organising here means putting into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O, the zero shape, is nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A philosophy of planning on a grand scale, never thinking small.
explanation.walkthrough: BIG, O and SMALL are rearranged, and the whole clue defines the outlook: arranging things on a world scale rather than a local one.
explanation.definitionFit: Globalism is a policy of planning on a worldwide rather than national or local scale.

clue.text: Something of importance from British government leader, in principle

indicators.note: in places the leader's letter inside the word for principle

parts.note: an ideal is a guiding principle

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of government

explanation.surface: An announcement from the head of the British government, in principle, is a matter of note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'government leader' looks like the prime minister but gives only G, which goes inside IDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A big deal is a matter of great importance, as in 'it's no big deal'.

clue.text: Musical piece unknown in 60% of orchestras, oddly

indicators.note: in puts the unknown inside the rearranged letters
oddly means strangely arranged, so the selected letters are rearranged
60% of a ten-letter word is its first six letters

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A mysterious piece that most orchestras have never heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: '60% of orchestras' gives ORCHES; 'oddly' rearranges it to SCHERO, and Z goes 'in'. 'oddly' is not alternate letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively movement in a symphony or sonata, a musical piece.

clue.text: See 12
Support advocate primarily put in place

definitions.text: Support advocate primarily put in place

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter of advocate

parts.note: laid means set down or put in place

explanation.surface: Help is given so a lawyer can be appointed for a case.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the scheme: state support that puts an advocate in place for someone who cannot pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal aid is public funding that provides a lawyer for those unable to afford one.

clue.text: See 6
Unsuccessful kind of situation currently at one's office

parts.note: now means at present, currently
in means at work, as in 'is the boss in?'

explanation.surface: Things are going badly for someone at work at the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one where every possible outcome is a failure.

clue.text: Some Africans have seen eagles flying around

indicators.note: flying around suggests birds wheeling about, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tourists in Africa have watched eagles circling overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying around' rearranges SEEN EAGLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegalese people come from Senegal, a country in West Africa.

clue.text: The second part of what you're doing makes news

definitions.text: The second part of what you're doing
definitions.meaning: the solver is doing a crossword
... means news or tidings, as in 'any ... from them?'

explanation.surface: Doing something, someone gets news halfway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what you're doing' is solving a crossword, which ends in this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Word can mean news or a message, as in 'send word' or 'the word is out'.

clue.text: Rattle badly with surprise, initially?

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of surprise
badly says the letters of the word rattle are put in a poor order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is badly shaken by something unexpected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the word rattle, after the first letter of 'surprise'; read as a whole, the clue also defines the answer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to alarm or rattle someone with a sudden surprise.

clue.text: Block on name of former president

parts.note: a clint is a block of limestone in a limestone pavement, between the fissures called grikes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ban placed on a former head of state's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Block' looks like a ban but is a geology word for a slab of limestone. Bill Clinton was US president from 1993 to 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinton is the surname of Bill Clinton, the 42nd US president.
